title: Finite two-root charts of the relative Fermat hypersurface
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $n\geq1$ be an integer, and let $D_n\subset\mathbf P^2_S$ be the closed subscheme defined by the homogeneous equation $A^n-B^n-C^n=0$ [def-pc-proj, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-pc-zero-scheme, def-pc-projective-space-twist]. The opens $D_+(C)\cap D_n$ and $D_+(A)\cap D_n$ cover $D_n$. There is a unique $S$-morphism $q_n:D_n\to\mathbf P^1_S$ with inverse images of the standard target charts $\mathbf A^1_S(x)$ and $\mathbf A^1_S(y)$ equal to those two opens, respectively, and with $x=(A/C)^n$ and $y=(C/A)^n$ there. On every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, its two chart rings, as algebras over the indicated target chart rings, are
$$S_C=R[x,a,b]/(a^n-x,b^n-(x-1)),\qquad S_A=R[y,u,v]/(v^n-y,u^n-(1-y)),$$
where $a=A/C$, $b=B/C$, $u=B/A$, $v=C/A$. The overlap substitutions are $v=a^{-1}$, $u=b/a$, $y=x^{-1}$. The $R[x]$-module $S_C$ has basis $\{a^ib^j:0\leq i,j<n\}$ and the $R[y]$-module $S_A$ has basis $\{u^iv^j:0\leq i,j<n\}$ (basis means that every element has a unique finite linear combination in these monomials). The morphism $q_n$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective on all scheme points. These chart descriptions, overlap maps and the morphism commute with every base change $T\to S$: $D_n\times_ST$ is the closed hypersurface $A^n-B^n-C^n=0$ in $\mathbf P^2_T$, with the displayed charts and maps over $T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. No normality, reducedness, characteristic, invertibility or roots-of-unity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BYA, section-plane-curves, standard affine pieces of the Fermat equation; explicit relative chart, gluing, two monic power bases and residue-field lifting arguments of returned lem-sfb-fermat-kummer-relative-curve proof steps 1--3, extended to arbitrary positive n.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] over each affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$. On the $C$-chart the twist $\mathcal O(n)$ has frame $C^n$ by [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so the coefficient of the defining section is $a^n-b^n-1$. The local zero-scheme formula [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties] gives $R[a,b]/(a^n-b^n-1)$. Likewise the $A$-chart has ring $R[u,v]/(1-u^n-v^n)$. The ambient three standard charts cover. A point outside both the $A$- and $C$-charts would lie on the $B$-chart with $A/B=C/B=0$ in its residue field; the equation there would give $-1=0$. Thus the two claimed opens cover, without any reducedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), Tag 01MS (lemma-when-invertible); zero scheme as in divisors.tex, lemma-zero-scheme; explicit dehomogenization of curves.tex Tag 0BYA.

proof.text: On their intersection, the degree-zero fraction restrictions of [def-pc-proj] give $v=C/A=a^{-1}$ and $u=B/A=b/a$. Indeed inverting $a$ in the first chart gives $R[a,a^{-1},b]/(a^n-b^n-1)$; substituting $v=a^{-1},u=b/a$ sends $1-u^n-v^n$ to $(a^n-b^n-1)/a^n=0$. Conversely $a=v^{-1},b=u/v$ sends the first equation to $(1-u^n-v^n)/v^n=0$. The substitutions are inverse on every generator, including coefficients of $R$. These formulas agree under restriction to every smaller affine base open, since the homogeneous fractions are the same sections.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] applied to $\mathbf P^1_S$, over each affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ the standard target charts are $\operatorname{Spec}R[x]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R[y]$, with $y=x^{-1}$ on their overlap. Define maps from the two source opens to these charts by $x\mapsto a^n$ and $y\mapsto v^n$. On affine base pieces these ring maps give scheme morphisms by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; they agree on base overlaps because $a=A/C$ and $v=C/A$ are global chart sections. Glue over $S$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. On the intersection, $v^n=a^{-n}$, so the two maps agree under the target transition $y=x^{-1}$, again the standard fractions of [def-pc-proj]. Glue once more to obtain $q_n$. In the $A$-chart, lying in the other target chart means $y=v^n$ is invertible, equivalent to $v$ invertible, hence to membership in the $C$-chart. The reverse assertion uses $x=a^n$ in the same way. Thus the inverse images are exactly the stated opens. Any morphism satisfying the specified formulas agrees on this cover, so the same gluing uniqueness proves uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 01I2 (lemma-category-affine-schemes), Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors), morphism gluing; target overlaps from constructions.tex Tag 01NG.

proof.text: Adjoin a redundant coordinate $x=a^n$ in the $C$-chart: the map from $R[x,a,b]/(a^n-x,b^n-(x-1))$ to $R[a,b]/(a^n-b^n-1)$ sends $x$ to $a^n$ and fixes $a,b$. Its inverse fixes $a,b$, and the relations make both composites identity. Similarly $y=v^n$ identifies the $A$-chart with the displayed $S_A$. The overlap of step 2 therefore also satisfies $y=v^n=a^{-n}=x^{-1}$. For $S_C$, apply [lem-sfb-monic-quotient-faithful-tensor-coordinates] first to $R[x][a]/(a^n-x)$ and then, over that ring, to $b^n-(x-1)$. Each element has a unique expression $\sum_{j<n}(\sum_{i<n}r_{ij}a^i)b^j$, with $r_{ij}\in R[x]$: uniqueness follows first in the $b$-basis, then in the $a$-basis. This is exactly the claimed product basis. For $S_A$ first adjoin $u$ with $u^n=1-y$, then $v$ with $v^n=y$, and repeat. The cited lemma includes the zero ring and uses the specified positive integer $n$, so no polynomial-degree claim over the zero ring is needed.

source.place: Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of (10) implies (1), monic quotient finite free; Tag 00HB (definition-flat), positive-rank monic quotients; two successive applications and coefficient comparison.

proof.text: Over the two target charts above each affine base open, step 3 identifies the inverse images with the affine schemes of step 4. Each coordinate algebra is generated as a module by its $n^2$ basis monomials, hence its structural ring map is finite. These target affines cover $\mathbf P^1_S$ by clauses (a) and (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Applying condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] proves that $q_n$ is finite in the precise sense of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], even when $S$ has no finite affine cover.

Each of the two successive monic quotient maps in step 4 is faithfully flat by [lem-sfb-monic-quotient-faithful-tensor-coordinates], since $n\geq1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] separately to the two maps: every prime of $R[x]$ lifts first to a prime of $R[x][a]/(a^n-x)$ and then to a prime of $S_C$. Their composite contraction is the original prime, so the $C$-chart map is surjective on all points. The same two lifts using $u,v$ prove surjectivity over the $y$-chart. Since the target charts over all affine base opens cover, every point of $\mathbf P^1_S$ has a preimage under $q_n$. This argument includes inseparable and nonreduced charts; over an empty base it is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), (1) implies (2), applied twice; Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), finite free monic quotient.

proof.text: For a ring map $R\to R'$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] computes affine base change by tensor product. Explicitly, $R'\otimes_R R[a,b]/(a^n-b^n-1)\cong R'[a,b]/(a^n-b^n-1)$: send $r'\otimes\overline{P}$ to $r'\overline{P_{R'}}$; the inverse sends $r'$, $a$, $b$ to $r'\otimes1$, $1\otimes a$, $1\otimes b$. The relations vanish and both composites fix the generators, so this is an isomorphism with no flatness assumption. The identical generator argument works for the $A$-chart and both redundant-coordinate presentations. Projective space itself base-changes by the fibre-product definition [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] over $T$, the ambient charts of $\mathbf P^2_T$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R'$ are $\operatorname{Spec}R'[a,b]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R'[u,v]$, with the pulled-back coordinate sections. On these ambient charts the zero scheme of the pulled section has exactly these quotient rings by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties], using only its local formula. The overlap substitutions still send $v$ to $a^{-1}$, $u$ to $b/a$, and $y$ to $x^{-1}$, and the maps still send $x$ to $a^n$, $y$ to $v^n$, because scalar extension fixes these monomials and fractions. For an arbitrary $T\to S$, cover $T$ by affine opens mapping into affine opens of $S$; the computed isomorphisms agree on overlaps on coefficients and coordinates and hence glue uniquely by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. They identify the base-changed closed subscheme with the stated hypersurface and identify its morphism with $q_n$ over $T$.
